# Find an XUI icon

**Never write an `<svg>` for an icon. Search first.**

```
npx xui-find-icon settings
npx xui-find-icon "three dots menu"
node scripts/find-icon.mjs trash --all
```

Or, through MCP: the `find_xui_icon` tool, same index and the same ranking.

## Why this exists

XUI has **275 icons in four families** and — until this index — only 117 of them
were visible to anything reading the contract. The manifest listed Icons v2 and
the coin badges; the 158 general icons appeared nowhere. So an agent asked for a
"file" icon found nothing, concluded the system had none, and drew one.

That is not a hypothetical. Five component stories shipped hand-drawn `<svg>`s.
In one row of four, measured inside identical 20px boxes, the glyphs painted
between **45% and 94%** of their box — one of them overflowing it — so the row
read as ragged however precisely the component centred it. A human caught it by
eye; ten automated gates had passed it. The library's own glyphs measure 43–63%
because they came off one grid.

## The rule

1. **Search by meaning**, not by guessing a name. The names are Figma's layer
   names and they are inconsistent by inheritance — `ActionsIcon` and
   `MoreVertIcon` are the same idea in two families. Search `"kebab"`.
2. **Take the import line it gives you.** That is the whole output; do not
   retype the name from memory.
3. **If it returns nothing, that is the finding.** Report it to the user and
   record it on Guides > Status as a gap in the icon set. It is never licence to
   draw a replacement — `npm run check:story-icons` rejects an inline `<svg>` in
   any component story, and that gate exists because of the failure above.

## Things the search will tell you, and which matter

- **Family.** Prefer **Icons v2** — four tones, `currentColor`, follows the
  theme. Fall back to the **general icons** when v2 has no equivalent.
- **Coin badges are not general-purpose icons.** They are transaction-type
  artwork with a fixed raw-hex palette that does **not** follow the theme; they
  take `size` and ignore `color`. The search ranks them last for this reason.
- **Name collisions.** Figma reuses one name for different drawings, and code
  disambiguates with a `General` or numeric suffix — there are two `Dust`
  components, a `Lost` beside a `Lost1`, and `ArrowForward` in two families.
  When your result is one of these the search prints the others; check you took
  the one you meant.

## Keeping it honest

`xui.icons.json` is generated by `scripts/gen-icon-index.mjs` and rebuilt as
part of `npm run ds:build`, so it cannot drift from the exports. The curated
synonyms are hand-kept — and the generator **throws** if a synonym names an icon
that no longer exists, so a rename breaks the build instead of silently deleting
the only word anybody would have searched for.

Add a synonym when you searched for something reasonable and did not find the
icon that was sitting there all along. That is the signal; act on it.

Related: [[figma-icon-parity]] audits the icons against Figma.
[[component-showcase-stories]] covers what a story should look like once you
have the right icon.
